The geometric meaning of a vector dot product is the projection of one vector onto another. It is a scalar value that represents the amount of one vector that is parallel to another. The dot product of two vectors A and B is given by the formula:

A · B = |A| |B| cos(θ)

where |A| and |B| are the magnitudes of vectors A and B, and θ is the angle between them.

If A and B are orthogonal vectors, meaning they are perpendicular to each other, then cos(θ) = 0. In this case, the dot product is zero, and the vectors are perpendicular to each other.

If A and B are negative projections of each other, meaning one vector is the negative of the other, then cos(θ) = -1. In this case, the dot product is negative, and the vectors are pointing in opposite directions.

The dot product can also be used to find the angle between two vectors. If A and B are unit vectors (i.e., their magnitudes are 1), then the dot product is simply the cosine of the angle between them. For example, if A · B = 0.5, then the angle between A and B is 60 degrees.

In summary, the geometric meaning of a vector dot product is the projection of one vector onto another, and it can be used to find the angle between two vectors and to determine if two vectors are orthogonal or negative projections of each other.
